chunks: There is no distinction higher than Islam; no honour more honourable than fear of Allāh; no asylum better than self restraint; no intercessor more effective than repentance; no treasure more precious than contentment; and no wealth is a bigger remover of destitution than being satisfied with mere sustenance. He who confines himself to what is just enough for maintenance achieves comfort and prepares abode in ease. Desire is the key of grief and the conveyance of distress. Greed, vanity and jealousy are incentives to falling into sins and mischief-mongering is the collection of all bad habits.

key_terms.بُلْغَةُ الْكَفَافِ: Balaghat al-kafaf (what is just enough for maintenance)

ai.seo_question: What are the highest virtues and moral qualities according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) synthesizes ethical theology with practical asceticism, framing wara' (scrupulousness) not merely as restraint but as a spiritual fortress against sin. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on inner purity (taqwa) as the true measure of nobility, contrasting worldly accumulation with the spiritual wealth of qana'ah (contentment). The warning against greed and arrogance underscores the moral decay that leads to transgression, aligning with the broader Islamic concept of self-purification (tazkiyah).
